Amsterdam is ⓐto wander along the canals, which
are lined with beautiful, historic buildings, and see a
wide variety of boats ⓑthat comes in all shapes,
sizes, and colors. Canals are the heart and soul of
Amsterdam, as they are the defining icons that
ⓒmake this city uniquely. With so many attractions
and such visual beauty, this is ⓓone of the world’s
greatest city to discover on foot or by boat. The
canal boat tours take about an hour and ⓔprovide
an excellent and unique way to experience the
waterways.

다음 글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓕ 중, 어법상 어색한 것을모두 골라 짝지은 것은?

“The Van Gogh Museum in Amsterdam”
Amsterdam is home to a lot of museums, but the
Van Gogh Museum was ⓐthe one I was really
excited to visit. The most interesting part of the
museum was the way the exhibits were arranged
ⓑto show how had the artist’s style changed over
time. The museum showed many of Vincent van
Gogh’s
most
well-known
works,
including
my
personal favorites: The Bedroom, Sunflowers, and
Wheatfield with Crows. The bright colors in The
Bedroom ⓒseemed to convey a sense of relaxation.
The different shades of yellow in Sunflowers ⓓwere
just amazing. In Wheatfield with Crows, the contrast
between the bright yellow wheat field and the cool
blue sky was striking. Overall, ⓔsee the artworks in
person was a very powerful experience.
The museum also displayed the letters that Van
Gogh wrote to his younger brother, Theo. Reading
those letters, I found out how much the artist loved
his brother. After I bought ⓕa few postcards with
Van Gogh’s art on them, I slowly cycled back to
the hotel. On my way back, I couldn’t help but
admire the beautiful, calm, and scenic views of the
city, especially people relaxing on the grass and
enjoying the sun.
solution: ⓑ had the artist’s style changed → the artist’s style had changed (완전한 절에 흐름상 ‘보여주기 위해서’라는 의미로 연결되어야 하므로 목적을 나타내는 부사적 용법의 to부정사 to show가 쓰인 것과, show의 목적어로 how가 이끄는 간접의문문이 쓰이 는 것은 적절하나, 간접의문문은 ‘의문사(구)+평서문’ 어순이므 로 의문부사 how(어떻게) 뒤에 ‘조동사+주어+과거분사’ 어순으 로 쓰인 had the artist’s style changed를 ‘주어+조동사+과거 분사’ 어순인 the artist’s style had changed로 고쳐야 한다.) ⓔ see → seeing[to see] (뒤에 술어동사 was가 따로 존재하므로 동사원형으로 시작하는 명령문이 되는 see는 알맞지 않으며, 주어 역할을 하는 동명사 (구)나 명사적 용법의 to부정사(구)를 이루도록 동명사 seeing 이나 to부정사인 to see로 고쳐야 한다.) 천재(강상구) 3과

I highly recommend visiting the Zaanse Schans
and Volendam if you want to get out of the busy
city to experience traditional Dutch culture. A trip
to the Netherlands wouldn’t be complete without a
visit to the windmills. Fortunately, you can get to
the
Zaanse
Schans,
which
is
famous
for
its
windmills,
in
just
17
minutes
by
train
from
Amsterdam.
The moment I saw the village, its beauty took my
breath away. Several windmills were spinning by the
river in the distance. Soon I felt like I was taken to
a point in the past. I looked into one of the
working windmills, and it was grinding nuts into oil
with its large stone wheels.
Near the windmills, I found a cheese farm and a
clog factory. I was surprised by the variety of Dutch
cheeses and actually a little unsure about tasting
them at first because they were mostly new to me.
However, when I tried some of them, they turned
out to be incredibly satisfying. I also tried on a few
pairs of clogs and (A)그것들이 꽤 편안하다는 것을
알게 되었는데, 이것을 나는 예상하지 못했었다.

∎James: The writer suggests visiting places where
you can experience traditional Dutch
culture like windmills.
∎Kate: Zaanse Schans is a bit far to reach by
train from Amsterdam.
∎Brian: The writer felt as if he/she had traveled
to the future while visiting the windmills.
∎Amy: When the writer peered inside a working
windmill, nuts were being ground by its
stone wheels.
∎Tom: The writer was unsure about trying Dutch
cheeses and ended up regretting tasting
them.
choices: James, Brian
James, Amy
Kate, Brian
Kate, Tom
Amy, Tom
solution: 글쓴이가 전통적인 네덜란드 문화를 경험하기 위해 풍차로 유 명한 잔서스한스를 방문할 것을 추천하고 있으므로, ‘글쓴이는 풍차와 같은 전통적인 네덜란드 문화를 경험할 수 있는 장소 들을 방문할 것을 제안하고 있어.’라고 설명한 James는 글의 내용을 잘 이해했다고 볼 수 있다. 글쓴이가 작동 중인 한 풍차를 들여다보니, 커다란 돌 바퀴로 견과류를 갈아서 기름을 만들고 있었다고 했으므로, ‘글쓴이가 작동 중인 풍차 안을 들여다보았을 때, 견과류가 그것의 돌 바 퀴에 의해 갈리고 있었어.’라고 설명한 Amy 역시 글의 내용을 잘 이해했다고 볼 수 있다.

@Olivia: I wonder if Dutch wooden shoes are comfortable.
What do YOU think?
@Liam: I have worn Dutch clogs, and I have to
admit they are rather comfortable and useful as
well. The wood keeps my feet dry. It easily absorbs
sweat and allows the feet to breathe. The wood
also provides good support and protects the feet.
(A)______________ they are perfect for activities like
gardening, farming, and walking in muddy areas.
@Katie: I tried wearing clogs during a visit to the
Netherlands, and I found them uncomfortable. The
wood was hard and inflexible, and my feet started
to hurt after a while.
@Jacob: After they’re worn frequently, or if you
wear thick socks, they’ll become more comfortable.
@Ashley: I have never worn clogs, but I believe they
are probably comfortable for people who are used
to them. Clogs have long been a part of Dutch
culture, especially in rural regions, and I’d love to
try a pair someday.
@Ethan: I purchased a pair of Dutch clogs during
my trip to the Netherlands, and I have to say they
are not the most comfortable shoes. (B)______________,
they do look very pretty and unique.

윗글의 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것은?

(A)         (B)           (A)      (B)
choices: SoThus
OrLikewise
SoHowever
YetThus
YetHowever
solution: (A) 나막신의 나무가 땀을 쉽게 흡수하고 발이 숨 쉴 수 있도 록 해주며, 좋은 지지력을 제공하고 발을 보호해 준다는 내용 다음에, 이를 통한 결론으로서 나막신이 정원 가꾸기, 농사일, 진흙길을 걷는 것과 같은 활동에 완벽하다는 내용이 이어지므 로, 빈칸에는 인과관계를 나타내는 접속사 ‘So(그래서)’가 알맞다. (B) 네덜란드 여행 중에 산 나막신이 가장 편안한 신발은 아니 었다는 내용 다음에, 나막신이 매우 예쁘고 독특해 보인다는 대조적인 내용이 이어지므로, 빈칸에는 역접의 접속부사 ’However(하지만)‘가 알맞다.

wouldn’t be complete without a visit to the

The moment I saw the village, its beauty took my
breath away. Several windmills were spinning by the
river in the distance. Soon I felt like I was taken to
a point in the past. I looked into one of the
working windmills, and it was grinding nuts into oil
with its large stone wheels.
Near the windmills, I found a cheese farm and a
clog factory. I was surprised by the variety of Dutch
cheeses and actually a little unsure about tasting
them at first because they were mostly new to me.
However, when I tried some of them, they turned
out to be incredibly satisfying. I also tried on a few
pairs of clogs and found them quite comfortable,
which I hadn’t expected.

(Telephone rings.)
M: Hello, thank you for calling City Hall. This is
Steve Kim speaking. How may I help you?
G: Hello, Mr. Kim. My name is Stella Bailey, and
I’m attending Norweech High School. (A)I was
wondering if you could help me find some
volunteer work for the city.
M: Sure! I’d be happy to help you, Stella! What
kind of work are you interested in?
G: I’m interested in environmental issues. Do you
have any suggestions?
M: What about joining the Urban Garden campaign?
G: That sounds interesting. Could you tell me more
about it?
M: It’s a campaign where local students come
together to create small gardens in urban
spaces. It helps make the city greener.
G: That’s a great way to support our community.
How can I join the campaign?
M: You can sign up on the City Hall website.
G: Great. Do I need any experience or special skills
to participate?
M: Not at all. The campaign is open to anyone
who wants to help. We’ll provide you with
everything you’ll need.
G: That’s cool! I’m really excited to get involved
and make a positive impact in the community.
Thank you for your help.
M: My pleasure! I’m glad to be of help.

윗글의 밑줄 친 (A)와 바꿔 쓸 수 없는 것은?
choices: Make sure that you
I'd like to ask you to
I was hoping you could
I’d appreciate it if you could
I'd like to know if you could

body:
The piece below, titled Homestead, is a painting
by Jon Ching. Most of his work, including this
painting, is a celebration of nature and a quiet
appeal to humans to appreciate the world around
them. “I believe we’ve separated ourselves from
nature and no longer see how we fit in. 자연이 번
성하도록 돕는 대신에, 우리는 그저 그것을 소비하고
있습니다,” says Ching.
One cannot help but smile at his paintings, which
are rich in color and tenderness. One of the fun
aspects of his work is how he blends the features
of one life form with those of another. “I’ve been
using my work as a means of commenting on
issues and problems I’m heavily interested in. I find
it necessary to express a silver lining rather than
just reflect on what’s wrong. I want to show that
everything is connected and that protecting nature
is actually protecting us. My call to action is to
remember the magic and wonder of this planet.”

Ching believes that humans have becomedisconnected from nature.
Ching's paintings are characterized by vibrantcolors and tenderness.
Ching uses his artwork to highlight problemsrather than focusing on the positive side.
Ching wants to remind people of the magic andwonder of the planet.

The piece below, titled Homestead, is a painting
by Jon Ching. Most of his work, including this
painting, is a celebration of nature and a quiet
appeal to humans to appreciate the world around
them. “I believe we’ve separated ⓐus from nature
and no longer see how we fit in. Instead of helping
nature thrive, we are simply consuming it,” says
Ching.
One cannot help but smile at his paintings, which
are rich in color and tenderness. One of the fun
ⓑaspect of his work is how he blends the features
of one life form with those of another. “I’ve ⓒbeen
using my work as a means of commenting on
issues and problems I’m heavily interested in. I find
ⓓit necessary to express a silver lining rather than
just reflect on ⓔwhat is wrong. I want to show that
everything is connected and that protecting nature
is actually protecting us. My call to action is to
remember the magic and wonder of this planet.”

December 21, 2018
Secretive street artist Banksy designed another
interesting piece of art, ⓐthat appears on a
concrete block garage in Port Talbot, Wales. It
shows a child catching snowflakes with his mouth.
When you look around the corner, however, you
realize that the child’s mouth is open to ash
ⓑcoming from a dumpster fire.
Banksy was asked by Gary Owen, a Port Talbot
resident, to create art ⓒthat would highlight Port
Talbot’s dust problem. Owen believed that the
area’s children were facing serious health risks by
playing in the dust coming from the local steel
plant.
Children are particularly defenseless against air
pollution. Since they have faster breathing rates
ⓓthan adults, they breathe in more pollutants.
According to the World Health Organization (WHO),
about 93% of the world’s children under 15 breathe
in toxic air every day. In 2016, the WHO even
estimated ⓔthat about 600,000 children died from
exposure to polluted air.
Banksy’s art has included environmental messages
before. For example, his 2010 artwork was created
at the remains of a plant in Detroit. It showed a
child with a can of red paint and the words, “I
remember when all this was trees.”
↳ I heard that both works of art ⓕhave been
moved to other places. - February 8, 2022

다음 글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓕ 중, 어법상 어색한 것을모두 골라 짝지은 것은?

The piece below, titled Homestead, is a painting
by Jon Ching. Most of his work, including this
painting, is a celebration of nature and a quiet
appeal to humans to appreciate the world around
them. “I believe we’ve separated ourselves from
nature and no longer see ⓐhow we fit in. Instead
of helping nature ⓑto thrive, we are simply
consuming it,” says Ching.
One cannot help but smile at his paintings, which
are rich in color and tenderness. One of the fun
aspects of his work ⓒis how he blends the features
of one life form with ⓓthat of another. “I’ve been
using my work as a means of commenting on
issues and problems ⓔwhich I’m heavily interested
in. I find it necessary to express a silver lining
rather than just reflect on what’s wrong. I want to
show
that
everything
is
connected
and
that
protecting nature is actually ⓕprotect us. My call to
action is to remember the magic and wonder of
this planet.”
solution: ⓓ that → those (앞서 언급된 복수명사구 the features(특징들)를 대신하므로, 복수대명사 those로 고친다.) ⓕ protect → protecting[to protect] (두 번째 that의 명사절에서 주어와 술어동사 is, 부사 actually 에 이어지는 주격보어 자리이므로, 명사의 역할을 하는 동명사 protecting이나 to부정사 to protect로 고친다.) 천재(강상구) 4과

In the middle of a major disaster, community
mapping can prove to be a very effective and
important tool. The first responders to a disaster
are often ordinary citizens.
(A) In response to this problem, a group of high
school students in New Jersey worked together

personal observations, calls to local gas stations,
and updates from other social media users. The

information gap.
(B) For example, community mapping helped deal

States. One of its main effects was energy
failures. Residents in affected areas would wait
for hours in line at gas stations, sometimes only
to learn that they were out of gasoline.
(C) They can use maps to create and update data
on health facilities, shelters, or even public
roads.
When
community
members
work
together at the time of a disaster, the gathered
information can be based on actual needs
rather than guesses. This is particularly critical
when every second counts.

Trees on private lands were found to be more
diverse than those on public lands. The two groups
of trees served different purposes, too. Trees on
private lands served functions such as providing
fruit, flowers, or beauty, and those on public lands
provided shade, regulated temperature, and fought

their regions and are of a different species from
their neighbors’ trees.

covered an old boom box with various shells, which

collective
action

The piece below, titled Homestead, is a painting
by Jon Ching. Most of his work, including this
painting, is a celebration of nature and a quiet
appeal to humans to appreciate the world around
them. “I believe we’ve separated ourselves from
nature and no longer see how we fit in. Instead of
helping nature thrive, we are simply consuming it,”
says Ching.
One cannot help but smile at his paintings, which
are rich in color and tenderness. One of the fun
aspects of his work is how he blends the features
of one life form with those of another. “I’ve been
using my work as a means of commenting on
issues and problems I’m heavily interested in. I find
it necessary to express a silver lining rather than
just reflect on what’s wrong. I want to show that
everything is connected and that protecting nature
is actually protecting us. My call to action is to
remember the magic and wonder of this planet.”
Art
can
strike
up
conversations
about
the
environment, but more importantly, it can also
make a great difference by inspiring us to take
action. The following words from Andy Warhol, an
American pop artist, ring especially true in this
context. “They always say time changes things, but
you actually have to change them yourself.”
choices: Jon Ching thinks that humans have fully embracednature and are helping it thrive.
Jon Ching tries to express negative aspects ofthe world by using his art.
Jon Ching‘s work aims to show that protectingnature is the same as protecting humanity.
Art can spark conversation about the environment,but it fails to motivate people to take action.
Andy Warhol believed change would naturallycome with time.
solution: ❶ Jon Ching은 인간이 자연을 충분히 받아들이며 그것이 번 성하도록 돕고 있다고 생각한다. (→ 자연에서 이탈했고 그것 을 그저 소비하고 있다고 생각함) ❷ Jon Ching은 자신의 예술을 이용하여 세상의 부정적인 면 들을 표현하려고 한다. (→ 자신이 관심 있는 것들을 비평하는 수단으로 작품을 이용하며, 잘못된 것보다는 밝은 희망을 표출 하는 것이 필요하다고 생각함) ❹ 예술은 환경에 대한 대화를 유발할 수 있지만, 사람들이 행동을 취하도록 동기 부여하는 것에는 실패한다. December 21, 2018
Secretive street artist Banksy designed another
interesting piece of art, which appears on a
concrete block garage in Port Talbot, Wales. It
shows a child catching snowflakes with his mouth.
When you look around the corner, however, you
realize that the child’s mouth is open to ash
coming from a dumpster fire.
Banksy was asked by Gary Owen, a Port Talbot
resident, ⓐcreating art that would highlight Port
Talbot’s dust problem. Owen believed that the area’s
children were facing serious health risks by playing
in the dust ⓑcoming from the local steel plant.
Children are particularly defenseless against air
pollution. Since they have faster breathing rates
than adults, they breathe in more pollutants.
According to the World Health Organization (WHO),
about 93% of the world’s children under 15
ⓒbreathe in toxic air every day. In 2016, the WHO
even estimated that about 600,000 children died
from exposure to polluted air.
Banksy’s art has included environmental messages
before. For example, his 2010 artwork ⓓcreated at
the remains of a plant in Detroit. It showed a child
with a can of red paint and the words, “I
remember ⓔwhen all this was trees.”
↳ I heard ⓕwhat both works of art had been
moved to other places. - February 8, 2022

Banksy’s Environmental Art and Its Message
The Impact of Air Pollution on Children‘s Health

The Pluses and Minuses of Living in an IndustrializedSociety

December 21, 2018
Secretive street artist Banksy designed another
interesting piece of art, which appears on a
concrete block garage in Port Talbot, Wales. It
shows a child catching snowflakes with his mouth.
When you look around the corner, however, you
realize that the child’s mouth is open to ash
coming from a dumpster fire.
Banksy was asked by Gary Owen, a Port Talbot
resident, to create art that would highlight Port
Talbot’s dust problem. Owen believed that the
area’s children were facing serious health risks by
playing in the dust coming from the local steel
plant.
Children are particularly defenseless against air
pollution. Since they have faster breathing rates
than adults, they breathe in more pollutants.
According to the World Health Organization (WHO),
about 93% of the world’s children under 15 breathe
in toxic air every day. In 2016, the WHO even
estimated that about 600,000 children died from
exposure to polluted air.
Banksy’s art has included environmental messages
before. For example, his 2010 artwork was created
at the remains of a plant in Detroit. It showed a
child with a can of red paint and the words, “I
remember when all this was trees.”
↳ I heard that both works of art had been moved
to other places. - February 8, 2022
Banksy created two artworks addressing environmental
issues: the one in Port Talbot highlights the
health risks of air pollution for children, who are
particularly (A)_______________ to it due to their
faster breathing rates, and the other one in
Detroit depicts the (B)_______________ of nature.
(A)                  (B)
choices: susceptiblewonder
immunebeauty
vulnerableloss
indifferentdestruction
resistantdisappearance
solution: 정답은 ③ 이다. (해설 없음)

Before my trip to the Netherlands, 내가 그 나라에
대해 알았던 전부는 그곳이 풍차와 튤립으로 유명하다
는 것이었다. But as I cycled from place to place, I
experienced many things that I hadn’t expected,
and I wanted to share some of them with you.
“The Anne Frank House and the Prinsengracht in
Amsterdam”
My first stop was the Anne Frank House, one of
the old buildings lined up along the Prinsengracht,
a canal in Amsterdam. Since it was close to the
hotel I was staying at, I decided to rent a bike to
go there. I enjoyed riding along the canal. The
Anne Frank House is one of the most visited
museums in the Netherlands. It housed the secret
hiding place of Anne Frank.

choices: While traveling in the Netherlands, the writermoved from location to location by bike.
The writer had many unexpected experiencesduring the trip.
The first place the writer visited was the AnneFrank House.
The writer rented a bike to go to the AnneFrank House and had fun riding along the canal.
The Anne Frank House is considered one of theleast popular museums in the Netherlands.

“The Van Gogh Museum in Amsterdam”
Amsterdam is home to a lot of museums, but the
Van Gogh Museum was the one I was really excited
to visit. The most interesting part of the museum
was the way the exhibits were arranged to show
how the artist’s style had changed over time.
The museum showed many of Vincent van Gogh’s
most well-known works, including my personal
favorites: The Bedroom, Sunflowers, and Wheatfield
with Crows.
The bright colors in The Bedroom seemed to
convey a sense of relaxation. The different shades
of yellow in Sunflowers were just amazing. In
Wheatfield with Crows, the contrast between the
bright yellow wheat field and the cool blue sky was
striking. Overall, ________________________________________
was a very powerful experience.

December 21, 2018
Secretive street artist Banksy designed another
interesting piece of art, which appears on a
concrete block garage in Port Talbot, Wales. It
shows a child ⓐcatching snowflakes with his mouth.
When you look around the corner, (A)_____________,
you realize ⓑthat the child’s mouth is open to ash
coming from a dumpster fire.
Banksy was asked by Gary Owen, a Port Talbot
resident, ⓒcreate art that would highlight Port
Talbot’s dust problem. Owen believed that the area’s
children were facing serious health risks by playing
in the dust coming from the local steel plant.
Children are particularly defenseless against air
pollution. Since they have faster breathing rates
than adults, they breathe in more pollutants.
According to the World Health Organization (WHO),
about 93% of the world’s children under 15 breathe
in toxic air every day. In 2016, the WHO even
estimated that about 600,000 children died from
exposure to ⓓpolluted air.
Banksy’s art ⓔhas included environmental messages
before. (B)_____________, his 2010 artwork was created
at the remains of a plant in Detroit. It showed a
child with a can of red paint and the words, “I
remember when all this was trees.”
↳ I heard that both works of art had been moved
to other places. - February 8, 2022

The first responders to a disaster are often ordinary
citizens. They can use maps to create and ⓐupdate
data on health facilities, shelters, or even public
roads. When community members work together at
the time of a disaster, the gathered information
ⓑcan be based on actual needs rather than guesses.
This is particularly critical when every second counts.
For example, ⓒcommunity mapping helped to deal
with the impact of Hurricane Sandy, one of the
most destructive hurricanes to hit the United States.

Residents in affected areas would wait for hours in
line at gas stations, sometimes ⓔonly to learn that
they were out of gasoline. In response to this
problem, a group of high school students in New
Jersey
worked
together

an
online
community map, ⓕbeing published information on

solution: (A) 앞에서 중대 재난의 한가운데에서 재난에 대해 처음 대응 하는 사람들이 참여형 지도를 이용해 보건 시설, 대피소, 공공 도로에 대한 데이터를 만들고 갱신할 수 있다고 했으며, 매초 가 중요할 때 이것이 특히 결정적이라는 내용이 뒤에 이어지 므로, 재난의 시기에 공동체 구성원들이 함께 일할 때, 수집된 정보가 실제 필요에 기반해야 함을 언급하는 흐름이 자연스럽 다. 따라서 ‘actual needs(실제 필요)’가 알맞다. (C) 허리케인 샌디의 주요한 영향 중 하나로 연료 부족이 앞에 언급되었고, 뒤에는 고등학교 학생들이 온라인 참여형 지도를 만들어 이용 가능한 연료가 있는, 문을 연 주유소에 대한 정보 를 공개했다는 내용이 대책으로 언급되므로, 연료 부족의 문제 에 대한 구체적 설명으로 피해 지역의 주민들이 주유소에서 몇 시간씩 줄을 서서 기다렸지만 결국 휘발유가 바닥난 것을 알게 되었다는 흐름이 자연스럽다. 따라서 ‘out of(바닥난)’가 알맞다. 천재(강상구) 2과

In the middle of a major disaster, community

important tool. The first responders to a disaster are
often ordinary citizens. They can use maps to create
and update data on health facilities, shelters, or
even public roads. When community members work

information can be based on actual needs rather
than guesses. This is particularly critical when every
second ⓒcount.
For example, community mapping helped deal with
the impact of Hurricane Sandy, one of the most
destructive hurricanes ⓓto hit the United States.
One of its main effects was energy failures.
Residents in affected areas would wait for hours in
line at gas stations, sometimes only to learn that
they were out of gasoline. In response to this
problem, a group of high school students in New
Jersey
worked
together
to
create
an
online
community map, ⓔpublished information on open
gas stations with available fuel. The students
gathered information from personal observations,
calls to local gas stations, and updates from other
social media users. The live data streams filled a
significant community information gap.

“The Cube Houses in Rotterdam”
After being completely destroyed during World
War II, Rotterdam was restored into a beautiful port
city. Experimental and artistic constructions were
used to improve the appearance of the city. The
Cube Houses in Rotterdam are among the most
innovative buildings in the country. The bright
yellow houses were something I had been looking
forward to seeing, and 그것들은 내가 기대했었던 만
큼 환상적이었다.
One of the key features of the Cube Houses is
that the cubes are tilted by 45 degrees. I visited
the Show Cube Museum to get a feel of what life
in such a house was like. From the outside, it
looked entirely twisted, but once I went inside, it
was surprisingly quite comfortable.
For the last few days after the trip, I haven’t been
able to get the charming sights of the Netherlands
out of my mind. If you ever plan to visit the
country, I really hope that you will find my post
helpful.

간접의문문 의 어순이 ‘의문사(구)+평서문’ 형태이므로, 의문사 what 다음에 주어인 life를 먼저 쓴다. • <조건>에 must가 있으므로, ‘~였음이 틀림없다’라는 뜻 으로 과거에 대한 추측을 나타내는 표현인 ‘must have+ 과거분사’를 사용해 must have been like를 쓰고, 이어서 ‘그들에게’라는 뜻의 for them을 쓴다. 17) ④: windmill → windmills (‘~들 중 하나’라는 뜻의 ‘one of+관사(the)+복수명사(구)’에 해당하므로 단수명사인 windmill을 복수명사인 windmills로 고쳐야 한다. 그 외, windmills(풍차)가 ‘작동하는’ 주체이므로 능동의 의 미를 지닌 현재분사 working이 정관사 the와 명사 windmill 사이에 쓰여 명사를 수식하는 것은 알맞다.) 오답 ⓐ 완전한 절(you want to get out of the busy city) 에 연결되며, 흐름상 ‘경험하기 위해서’라는 의미가 되 어야 하므로 ‘목적’을 나타내는 부사적 용법의 to부정 사인 to experience는 알맞다. ⓑ 주어인 Several windmills(여러 개의 풍차들)가 돌아 가는 주체이며 과거의 진행 중인 동작을 나타내므로 ‘be동사의 과거형+현재분사’에서 복수주어에 수일치 시킨 복수형 과거동사를 쓴 자동사 spin의 과거진행형 were spinning은 알맞다. ⓒ feel like는 ’~처럼 느끼다’라는 뜻이며 이때 like는 전 치사로 쓰여 명사(구)나 동명사(구)를 목적어로 취하거나 접속사로 쓰여 목적어로 명사절을 취할 수 있으므로, felt 뒤에 접속사 like가 쓰여 완전한 절(I was taken to a point in the past)을 목적어로 취하는 felt like는 알맞다. ⓔ a few 다음에는 가산복수명사(구)가 이어져야 하므 로 복수명사 pairs 앞에서 ’몇몇의 ~‘를 뜻하는 a few 가 쓰인 것은 알맞다. 18) ④: (A) 다행히도, 풍차로 유명한 잔서스한스에 암스테르담 에서 기차로 17분 만에 도착할 수 있다는 내용이 뒤에 이어지므로, 풍차를 방문하지 않으면 네덜란드 여행이 완성되지 않는다는 흐름이 자연스럽다. 따라서 ‘incomplete(미완성의)’가 알맞다. complete 완전한 본문변형 wouldn’t be complete → would be incomplete (B) 글쓴이가 네덜란드 치즈의 다양한 종류에 놀랐으며 처음에 맛을 봐야 할지 확신이 별로 없었다고 했으므 로, 그 이유로 대부분의 치즈가 처음 보는 것이었다는 흐름이 자연스럽다. 따라서 ‘new(새로운)’가 알맞다. familiar 익숙한 (C) 글쓴이가 다양한 네덜란드 치즈를 맛보는 것에 대 해 확신이 별로 없었다는 내용 다음에 역접의 접속부 사 However(하지만)로 연결해 글쓴이가 몇 가지 치즈 를 먹어본 소감이 이어지므로, 그것들이 매우 맛있었다 는 흐름이 자연스럽다. 따라서 ‘satisfying(만족스러운)’ 이 알맞다. unsatisfying 만족스럽지 못한 19) they were as fantastic as I had expected : • 주어 they와 이에 수일치된 복수동사 were를 쓴 뒤, <조건>에 따라 ‘as+형용사[부사]의 원급+as(~만큼 …한)’ 형태의 동등 비교 표현이 되도록 정도를 나타내는 부사 as와 형용사 fantastic을 주격보어로 쓴다. • 두 번째 as는 전치사나 접속사로 쓰일 수 있으며, 여기 서는 뒤에 ‘내가 기대했었던 것’이라는 의미가 되어야 하 므로 접속사로 as를 쓴 뒤 비교 대상을 완전한 절의 형 태로 연결한다. 명사절의 주어로 I를 쓴 뒤, ‘기대했던’ 것 은 주절보다 더 과거에 일어난 일을 나타내므로 expect 를 expected로 변형해 ‘had+과거분사’ 형태의 과거완료 인 had expected를 쓴다. 20) ③: 글쓴이는 큐브 하우스가 겉으로는 완전히 뒤틀려 보였 지만, 안으로 들어가 보니 놀랍게도 꽤 편안했다고 했 으므로, ③ ‘글쓴이는 큐브 하우스가 겉에서 보이는 것 과 같이 불편하다는 것에 놀라지 않았다.’는 글의 내용 과 일치하지 않는다. 오답 ① 로테르담은 제2차 세계대전 중에 파괴되었지만 나중 에 복원되었다. ② 큐브 하우스의 큐브들은 45도 기울어져 있고, 이는 그것들을 특별하게 만든다. ④ 글쓴이는 여행 후 네덜란드의 아름다운 경치에 대해 계속 생각하고 있다. ⑤ 글쓴이는 자신의 게시물이 네덜란드를 방문할 계획이 있는 다른 사람들에게 도움이 되기를 진심으로 바란다.

“The assignment is to write a speech about
someone who you admire. It could be a historical
figure, a celebrity, or even someone you personally
know in your life,” Ms. Harper told the class. My
classmates began brainstorming a list of people
they might pick —  mostly athletes, singers, and

A few days later, Ms. Harper talked about how to

would have to give in front of my classmates! The

body:
The next day, I met Ms. Harper after school to
talk about the speech. I said, “I’m embarrassed
about the speech. (A)저는 정말 바보처럼 보였음이
틀림없어요. I know I could have done better.”
“It’s quite all right to fall short of your own
expectations as long as you learn something from
it,” she said in a warm voice. “What was bothering
you the most while you prepared for the speech?”
“I was afraid the other students would laugh at
me if my speech wasn’t good enough.” She replied,
“You certainly can’t control what others think about
your speech. That means you should be focusing
on the one thing you can control  —  how you give
your speech.” That woke me up from the depths of
despair. Of course, that was it! I wouldn’t have
been able to make my classmates like what I
wanted to say. I really should have focused on my
performance.

윗글의 주제로 알맞은 것은?
choices: power of controlling your emotions
importance of overcoming stage fright
aspect of a speech you should truly focus on
tips for delivering a speech that everyone willenjoy
impact of others' opinions on personal performance
solution: 로건은 다른 학생들의 반응에 신경을 쓰느라 지난 연설을 제 대로 못했지만, 남들이 자신의 연설을 어떻게 생각하는지는 통 제할 수 없기 때문에 연설을 어떻게 하는지에 초점을 맞춰야 한다는 하퍼 선생님의 말을 듣고 무엇이 문제였는지 깨닫는다. 따라서 글의 주제로 ❸ ‘연설에서 진정으로 집중해야 할 부분’ 이 알맞다. 천재(강상구) 1과

body:
A couple of weeks later, the class was given
another speech assignment. I didn’t want to drop
the ball like the first time. So this time, I practiced
delivering the speech. I stood in front of the mirror
every day for a week and went over all the things I
wanted to say. I used cue cards (A)[containing /
contained] key phrases about important facts. I
rehearsed how I would stand, how I would make
eye contact with the audience, and even when I
would pause.
I felt nervous again when the big day finally
arrived. But when the teacher called my name, I
noticed that my nerves had actually calmed down a
bit. I felt way better than the last time, for sure! I
walked up to the front of the class and looked out
into the audience. My heart began to race, and I
took a deep breath to calm (B)[down it / it down].
While my voice trembled from time to time, I
managed (C)[getting / to get] my whole message
across. When I was done, I felt so proud of myself
that I barely noticed how loudly everyone was
clapping for me!

윗글의 괄호 (A)~(C)에서 어법상 알맞은 말로 바르게 연결된 것은?

(A)
(B)
(C)
choices: containingdown itgetting
containedit downto get
containeddown itgetting
containingit downgetting
containingit downto get
solution: (A) 앞의 명사구인 cue cards를 수식하는 분사 자리인데, cue cards와 동사 contain(포함하다)이 능동 관계를 이루므로 현재 분사 containing의 수식을 받는 것이 알맞다. (B) ’calm ~ down’은 ‘~을 진정시키다‘를 뜻하는 구동사이며, 목적어가 대명사일 경우 동사와 부사 사이에 와야 하므로, calm it down이 알맞다. (C) manage는 to부정사를 목적어로 취하여 ‘간신히[그럭저럭] ~하다’라는 의미를 나타내므로, managed의 목적어 자리에는 to get이 알맞다.

(A)[Imagine / To imagine] you are giving a
presentation in class. As you stand before the class,
you see the following: A student in the front row is
texting on his cell phone. Two students in the
corner (B)[is / are] laughing over something they
are holding under their desks. Another student
seems (C)[working / to be working] on her

choices: Imagineareworking

solution: (A) 뒤에 술어동사가 따로 존재하지 않으므로, 동사원형으로 시작하는 명령문이 되는 Imagine이 알맞다. (B) 주어부 ‘Two students in the corner’에 이어진 문장의 동 사 자리로, 주어의 핵인 Two students가 복수명사이므로, 이에 수 일치된 복수동사 are가 알맞다. (C) seem은 ‘~인 것 같다’라는 뜻의 2형식 문장에서 to부정사 를 주격보어로 취하며 뒤에 진행형이 올 경우에는 to be를 생 략할 수 없으므로, to be working이 알맞다. 천재(강상구) 1과

body:
Good listeners can help speakers by creating a
positive communication ⓐclimate. As a listener, you
should listen carefully and look for something in
the speech that ⓑinterests you. Even if you are not
excited about the topic, you may pick up some
techniques that will be useful when it is your time
to speak. When you discuss or ⓒevaluate others’
speeches, be ⓓconstructive. That is an attitude you
will ⓔappreciate when others comment on your
speech.
(A)______________________________________________________
Fortunately, anyone can become a better listener.
Just remember the Golden Rule of Listening: Listen
to others as you would want them to listen to you.

윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ의 영영풀이로 알맞지 않은 것은?
choices: ⓐclimate: an atmosphere or a situation that existsin a particular place
ⓑinterest: to cause someone to want to learnmore about something or to becomeinvolved in something
ⓒevaluate: to judge the value or condition ofsomeone or something in a carefuland thoughtful way
ⓓconstructive: having a negative and unhelpfuleffect rather than being useful
ⓔappreciate: to be grateful for something
solution: constructive는 ‘건설적인’이라는 뜻이나, ‘having a negative and unhelpful effect rather than being useful(유용하기보다는 부 정적이고 도움이 안 되는 영향을 끼치는)’은 constructive의 반 의어인 destructive(파괴적인)에 대한 영영풀이이므로 알맞지 않다. ’helping to develop or improve something(뭔가를 발달 시키거나 향상시키는 데 도움을 주는)‘과 같은 설명으로 고쳐 야 한다.

body:
I was sweating as I walked up to the front of the
class. My heart was racing so fast ⓐthat I thought
it might fly out of my chest. I could feel my face
turning red. I didn’t know where to look. I blanked
out. I just stood there silently.
Ms. Harper tried to help me out. “ⓑStarting by
telling us a bit about your grandmother, Logan.” I
spoke about what kind of work my grandmother
used to do, but I quickly ran out of words ⓒto
say. Then Ms. Harper said, “How about telling us a
bit about why you admire her so much?” I barely
managed ⓓsharing a short story about her. After
that, I just rushed to my seat and put my head in
my hands. I knew I had messed up. I hadn’t said
all the things ⓔwhich I wanted to say.

윗글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
choices: Logan felt extremely nervous before giving thespeech.
Logan struggled with his speech and ended upspeechless.
Ms. Harper encouraged Logan to talk aboutwhy he admires his grandmother.

A couple of weeks later, the class was given another
speech assignment. I didn’t want to drop the ball
like the first time. (A)__________ this time, I practiced
delivering the speech. I stood in front of the mirror
every day for a week and went over all the things I
wanted to say. I used cue cards which contained
key phrases about important facts. I rehearsed how
I would stand, how I would make eye contact with
the audience, and even when I would pause.
I felt nervous again when the big day finally
arrived. But when the teacher called my name, I
noticed that my nerves had actually calmed down a
bit. I felt way better than the last time, for sure! I
walked up to the front of the class and looked out
into the audience. My heart began to race, and I
took a deep breath to calm it down. (B)____________
my voice trembled from time to time, I managed to
get my whole message across. When I was done, I
felt so proud of myself that I barely noticed how
loudly everyone was clapping for me!

다음 글의 제목으로 알맞은 것은?

Imagine you are giving a presentation in class. As
you stand before the class, you see the following: A
student in the front row is texting on his cell
phone. Two students in the corner are laughing
over something they are holding under their desks.
Another student seems to be working on her
homework. Finally, here is a student who seems
ready to listen. He has a supportive look on his
face; he is actually waiting for you to give your
presentation. Who would you like to have as your
listener?
Good listeners can help speakers by creating a
positive communication climate. As a listener, you
should listen carefully and look for something in
the speech that interests you. Even if you are not
excited about the topic, you may pick up some
techniques that will be useful when it is your time
to speak. When you discuss or evaluate others’
speeches, be constructive and helpful. That is an
attitude you will appreciate when others comment
on your speech.
Listening well is as important as speaking well.
Fortunately, anyone can become a better listener.
Just remember the Golden Rule of Listening: Listen
to others as you would want them to listen to you.
choices: How to Improve Speaking Skills
Managing Distractions in the Classroom
The Value of Feedback in Public Speaking
Effective Ways to Become a Good Listener
Listening vs. Speaking: Which Is More Important?

thought it might fly out of my chest. I could feel
my face turning red. ⓑI didn’t know where to look.
I blanked out. I just stood there silently.

us a bit about your grandmother, Logan.” I spoke
about ⓒwhat kind of work my grandmother was
used to do, (A)_________________________________________.

about why you admire her so much?” I barely
managed to share a short story about her. After
that, I just rushed to my seat and ⓓput my head
in my hands. I knew I had messed up. I hadn’t said
all the things I wanted to say.

talk about the speech. I said, “I’m embarrassed
about the speech. ⓔI must look like a fool. I know
I could have done better.”

expectations as long as you learn something from
it,” she said in a warm voice. “What was bothering
you the most while you prepared for the speech?”
“I was afraid the other students would laugh at
me if my speech wasn’t good enough.”
She replied, “You certainly can’t control what
others think about your speech. That means you
should be focusing on ⓕthe one thing which you
can control  —  how you give your speech.”

actors. However, I knew right away who my speech
was going to be about. Grandma is the person I
admire the most. Writing a speech about her would
be a piece of cake.

choose anyone they admire, whether
famous or not.

choosing a celebrity to write about.

The next day, I met Ms. Harper after school to
talk about the speech. I said, “I’m embarrassed
about the speech. I must have looked like a fool. I
know I could have done better.”
“It’s quite all right to fall short of your own
expectations as long as you learn something from
it,” she said in a warm voice. “What was bothering
you the most while you prepared for the speech?”
“I was afraid the other students would laugh at
me if my speech wasn’t good enough.”
She replied, “You certainly can’t control what
others think about your speech. That means you
should be focusing on the one thing you can
control  —  how you give your speech.” That woke
me up from the depths of despair. Of course, that
was it! (A)내가 나의 반 친구들에게 내가 말하고 싶었
던 것을 좋아하게 만들 수는 없었을 거야. I really
should have focused on my performance.

A couple of weeks later, the class was given
another speech assignment. I didn’t want to drop
the ball like the first time. So this time, I practiced
delivering the speech. I stood in front of the mirror
every day for a week and went over all the things I
wanted to say. I used cue cards ⓐwhich contained
key phrases about important facts. I rehearsed ⓑhow
I would stand, how I would make eye contact with
the audience, and even when I would pause.
I felt nervous again when the big day finally
arrived. But when the teacher called my name, I
noticed that ⓒmy nerves had actually calmed down
a bit. I felt way better than the last time, for sure! I
walked up to the front of the class and ⓓlook out
into the audience. ⓔMy heart began to race, and I
took a deep breath to calm it down. While my voice
trembled from time to time, I managed to get my
whole message across. When I was done, ⓕI felt too
proud of myself that I barely noticed how loudly
everyone was clapping for me!

윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓕ 중, 어법상 어색한 것을 모두골라 짝지은 것은?
solution: ⓓ look → looked 주어 I에 이어지는 과거동사 walked와 등위접속사 and로 병렬 연 결되어 있으므로, look을 과거형인 looked로 고쳐야 한다. ⓕ too → so ‘너무 ~해서 …하다‘라는 뜻으로, 부사 too의 뒤에는 결과 부사 절인 that 이하가 이어질 수 없으므로 ’so+형용사+that절‘이 되 도록 too를 so로 고쳐야 한다.

positive communication climate. As a listener, you
should listen carefully and look for something in
the speech that interests you. Even if you are not
excited about the topic, you may pick up some
techniques that will be useful when it is your time

to others as you would want them to listen to you.

느꼈다④ 나는 유명한 사람을 선택하고 싶었고, 마침내 결정을 내렸다⑤ 나는 내 가족 중 한 사람에 대해 쓰는 것을 고려했지만, 마음을 바꿨다17) ⑤: (A) 자신이 정말 바보처럼 보였을 것이며, 더 잘할 수있었던 걸 안다는 로건의 말이 이어지므로, 그가 연설에 부끄러움을 느낀다는 흐름이 자연스럽다. 따라서‘embarrassed(창피한)’가 알맞다.pleased 만족해하는(B) 하퍼 선생님이 따뜻한 목소리로 무언가를 배운다면전혀 괜찮다고 말했다는 내용이 이어지므로, 자신의 기대에 미치지 못하는 상황에 대해 언급했다는 흐름이자연스럽다. 따라서, ‘fall short of(~에 못 미치다)’가 알맞다.meet ~에 부응하다(C) 로건이 자신의 연설이 충분히 좋지 않으면 다른 학생들이 비웃을까 봐 두려웠다고 말하자, 하퍼 선생님은다른 사람들의 생각은 통제할 수 없기에 연설을 어떻게 하는지에 초점을 맞춰야 한다고 했으며 이를 통해그가 깨달음을 얻게 되므로, 그가 절망에서 빠져나왔다는 흐름이 자연스럽다. 따라서 ‘despair(절망)’가 알맞다.hope 희망18) ②: 연설을 주의 깊게 듣고 건설적인 평가의 태도를 취하는등 좋은 청중이 되는 법에 대해 설명하는 내용이므로,글의 목적으로 ② ‘더 나은 경청자가 되는 방법에 대해조언을 제공하기 위해’가 적절하다.오답① 학생들이 연설의 주제에 집중하도록 돕기 위해③ 학생들에게 연설을 건설적으로 평가하는 방법을 가르치기 위해④ 의사소통에서 말하기 기술의 중요성을 설명하기 위해⑤ 토론 중에 학생들이 더 명확하게 말하도록 격려하기위해19) (1) They[Good listeners] can help speakers by creating apositive communication climate.(2) They[Listeners] should be constructive and helpfulwhen evaluating others' speeches.질문(1) 좋은 청중은 연설 중에 어떻게 발표자를 도울 수 있는가?→ 그들[좋은 청중들]은 긍정적인 의사소통 분위기를 조성함으로써 발표자를 도울 수 있다.(2) 다른 사람의 연설을 평가할 때 청중들은 어떤 태도를지녀야 하는가?→ 그들[청중들]은 다른 사람의 연설을 평가할 때 건설적이고 도움이 되는 태도를 지녀야 한다.20) ⑤: 몇 주 후, 반에 또 다른 연설 과제가 주어졌으며, 글쓴이가 첫 번째처럼 망치고 싶어 하지 않았다는 내용의주어진 글에 이어, 이에 대한 결과로서 접속사 So(그래서)로 시작하여 글쓴이가 이번에는 연설 발표를 연습했다는 내용과, 일주일 동안 매일 거울 앞에 서서 할 말을 점검했으며 핵심 문구를 적은 큐카드를 사용했고,자세, 태도 등을 연습했다는 내용의 (C), (C)에서 언급된준비 기간이 지나고 연설 당일이 되었을 때, 글쓴이는긴장이 되었지만 자신의 이름이 불리자 지난번보다 훨씬 안정된 기분이었으며, 교실 앞쪽으로 가서 청중을바라보았다는 내용의 (B), (B)의 마지막에 언급된 관객앞의 상황에서 글쓴이가 긴장을 풀기 위해 심호흡을했으며, 떨리는 목소리로 전하고자 했던 메시지를 끝까지 전달하고 나자 글쓴이는 자신이 너무 자랑스러워서모두가 크게 박수치는 것도 잘 몰랐다는 내용의 (A)로이어지는 것이 알맞다.

body:
M: Look, Amy. I got these postcards of Leonardo
da Vinci’s paintings from the National Art
Museum yesterday.
W: The National Art Museum? Oh, they’re having the
Leonardo da Vinci exhibition. Did you enjoy it?
M: Very much. They also had a new AR docent
tour program, which was really interesting.
W: What is that about?
M: It gives you information on artwork using AR
technology. For example, if you scan a painting
with an app, it can show you a 3D version of it.
W: That’s pretty neat!
M: It can also provide a narration by a digital
version of the artist.
W: That must be exciting. How nice would it be if
future technology, like a time machine, could let
us talk with Leonardo da Vinci in person?
M: Yeah. Then, ________________________________________.
W: Why? What happened in 1503?
M: That’s the year he began painting the Mona
Lisa, my favorite painting. I could ask him about
the actual emotion of the model he wanted to
capture.
W: Who knows? Maybe time travel will be a reality
in the future. Let’s keep our fingers crossed.

위 대화의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것은?
choices: I believe he was born in 1503
I’d like to visit the museum again
I hope to see what it was like in 1500s
I wish I could go back in time to 1503
I wonder if AR technology is available at home
solution: 타임머신과 같은 미래의 기술이 레오나르도 다빈치와 직접 만 나서 대화할 수 있게 해준다면 정말 멋질 거라는 여자의 말에 동의하며 이어진 말로, 이에 대해 여자가 ‘왜?’라고 반응하면서 1503년에 무슨 일이 있었는지를 묻고 있으므로, 남자의 1503 년과 관련된 시간 여행에 대한 소망을 언급하는 흐름으로 빈 칸에는 ❹ ‘난 1503년으로 시간을 거슬러 올라갈 수 있으면 좋 겠어’가 알맞다.

body:
While thinking about her homework, Seoyoung Jun
closed one eye and (A)[successfully / hardly] picked
up her pencil holder. At that moment, she realized
that orienting herself in a 3D space didn’t require
both eyes. This surprised her. With research, she learned
that the brain can process 3D information without
any vision at all. And with that, the idea for a new
device for people with visual disabilities was born.
Those who have lost (B)[hearing / sight] get their
spatial information mainly from touch, not vision.
She based her new navigation device on this fact.
This little device sends a beam of infrared light to
gather 3D information about what may lie around
the user, including walls and furniture. The bounced
beam conveys that information to the device, which
then raises little pins to (C)[confuse / indicate]
where
those
obstacles
are.
By
“reading”
the
positions and heights of those pins, the user can
understand the arrangement of structures and
objects lying ahead and navigate around them.

윗글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 흐름상 알맞은 말로바르게 연결된 것은?

(A)
(B)
(C)
choices: successfully     sight    indicate
hardly     sight    indicate
successfully     hearing    indicate
hardly     hearing    confuse
successfully     sight    confuse
solution: (A) 3차원 공간에서 자기 위치를 인식하는 데에 양쪽 눈이 필 요하지는 않다는 것을 깨달았다는 내용이 이어지므로, 한쪽 눈 을 감은 채로 성공적으로 연필꽂이를 집어 들었다는 흐름으로 successfully(성공적으로)가 알맞다. (B) 시각 장애를 가진 사람들을 위한 새로운 장치에 대한 아이 디어가 탄생했다는 내용이 앞에 언급되었으므로, 시각을 잃은 사람들이 시각이 아니라 주로 촉각으로부터 공간에 대한 정보 를 얻는다는 흐름으로 sight(시력)가 알맞다. (C) 사용자가 올려진 핀들의 위치와 높낮이를 읽음으로써 앞에 놓인 구조물과 물체들의 배치를 파악한다는 내용이 이어지므 로, 장치가 작은 핀들을 올려 장애물이 있는 곳을 나타낸다는 흐름으로 indicate(나타내다, 보여주다)가 알맞다.

body:
The heart of this device is a 3D depth sensor
connected to a small computer. Seoyoung coded the
computer to control the nine motors ⓐ[line up /
lined up] in three rows of three so that each motor
could move a pin up and down.
(A) By running your hand over the nine pins, you
can tell where the obstacles are and how high
ⓑ[are they / they are].
(B) The sensor can scan eighteen blocks of space
before it, each 0.06㎥ in size.
(C) When it detects an obstacle in any of these
blocks, the corresponding pin rises to either the
middle or high position, depending on the
height of the obstacle.
When Seoyoung’s device worked for the first time,
she didn’t believe it. To be sure it wasn’t a mistake,
she shut it off and rebooted it. When it worked
again, she started screaming with joy. It ⓒ[has
been / had been] seven long months of research,
building, and testing. She imagines a future version
that could be connected to a smartphone, with
more pins and more height positions.

윗글의 괄호 ⓐ, ⓑ, ⓒ에서 어법상 알맞은 말로 바르게 연결된 것은?

ⓐ
ⓑ
ⓒ
choices: lined up  they are has been
line up  they are has been
lined up  are they had been
line up  are they had been
lined up  they are had been
solution: ⓐ 동사가 있는 완전한 절(Seoyoung coded ~ the nine motors)에 접속사 없이 다른 동사(구)가 이어질 수 없으므로, 흐름상 명사구 the nine motors를 수식하는 분사구를 이루어 야 하며, 수식받는 명사구 the nine motors가 타동사적 구동 사로 쓰인 line ~ up(~을 배열하다)의 대상이므로, 수동을 나 타내는 과거분사를 사용한 lined up이 알맞다. ⓑ how 이하는 동사 tell의 목적어인 where the obstacles are 와 등위접속사 and에 의해 병렬 연결된 간접의문문이므로 의 문사구 how high 뒤에 ‘주어+be동사’의 평서문 어순을 이루 는 they are가 알맞다. ⓒ 흐름상 장치가 다시 작동해서 그녀가 소리를 질렀던 과거 시점 이전까지 7개월간의 연구, 제작, 시험이 있었던 것이므 로, 과거완료(had+p.p) 시제의 had been이 알맞다.

Cars are now making steps toward their own kind
of freedom; that is, freedom from people. The goal
is ⓐto build a car that uses artificial intelligence so
that it thinks and drives like a human. The
technology for a self-driving car has reached the
point ⓑwhich it is becoming increasingly accessible.
Self-driving cars have clear advantages. Most of all,
sitting behind the wheel would no longer ⓒbe
limited by age or ability. For example, a person
who has lost sight could rely on a self-driving car
to go from one place to another. Furthermore,
most accidents are caused by careless people on
the road. For example, (A)많은 충돌들은 운전하는 동
안 휴대 전화를 사용하거나, 운전대를 잡고 졸거나, 또
는 취해 있는 동안 운전을 하는 사람들로 인해 발생된
다. With a self-driving car, people would not need
to worry about such situations on the road.
However, there are also some serious concerns
when it comes to (B)__________________________________,
since the technology is still far from perfect. In fact,
a self-driving car depends only on its sensors, GPS,
and computer programs ⓓwork properly. If any of
these broke down or were used for unintended
purposes, then the safety and security of the rider
as well as other people on the road  ⓔcan be put
at risk.

choices: the safety of autonomous cars
production costs of autonomous cars
equipping self-driving cars with robots
the economic impact of self-driving cars
environmental issues related to self-driving cars

Cars are now making steps toward their own kind
of freedom; that is, freedom from people. The goal
is to build a car that uses artificial intelligence so
that it thinks and drives like a human. The
technology for a self-driving car has reached the
point where it is becoming increasingly accessible.
Self-driving cars have clear advantages. Most of all,
sitting behind the wheel would no longer be limited
by age or ability. For example, a person who has
lost sight could rely on a self-driving car to go
from one place to another. Furthermore, most
accidents are caused by careless people on the
road. For example, many crashes are caused by
people using their phones while driving, falling
asleep at the wheel, or driving while drunk. With a
self-driving car, people would not need to worry
about such situations on the road.
However, there are also some serious concerns
when it comes to the safety of self-driving cars,
since the technology is still far from perfect. In fact,
a self-driving car depends only on its sensors, GPS,
and computer programs to work properly. If any of
these broke down or were used for unintended
purposes, then the safety and security of the rider
as well as other people on the road could be put
at risk.

clear, safety concerns remain because of their
(B)______________ technology.

today is Mr. Kim Deok-man. He’s here to talk
about yeot, an old Korean treat. Mr. Kim,
could you please ⓐintroduce yourself to our
viewers?
Mr. Kim: Sure. Hello, everyone! It’s great to be here.
I’m from Chungju, Korea, and specialize in
making yeot.
Host: Could you first tell us a little bit about yeot?
When did Koreans first ⓑstart enjoying it?
Mr. Kim: It is said that yeot dates back more than
1,000 years. Back in the old days, only the
rich could eat yeot, but nowadays, everyone
can enjoy it. It’s still popular.
Host: It has a ⓒlong history. Where did you learn
how to make yeot?
Mr. Kim: I learned it from my father and grandfather.
Our family has been making yeot for 140
years.

ⓓdescribe how to make it?

First, steamed rice is mixed with barley
malt and then fermented for several hours.
After that, it is boiled to make yeot batter.
The batter is then stretched and folded
back over and over again by hand. Lastly,
it is cut into small pieces.

your work?

ⓔnew
family
yeot
recipe

Aranmula, a village in India, is home to the
traditional craft of mirror making. Here, the mirrors
are made entirely of metal. With typical glass
mirrors, light has to travel through the glass in
order to get reflected on the back of the glass
coated with metal. In contrast, the Aranmula mirror
reflects light on the surface of the metal and shows
a more accurate reflection. The craft has been
passed down in Aranmula for around 500 years.
Sudhammal J learned the trade secrets from her
father when she was little, including the formula for
the perfect ratio of tin and copper to create the
mirror’s reflective surface.

I’m from Chungju, Korea, and specialize in
making yeot.
Host: Could you first tell us a little bit about yeot?
When did Koreans first ⓑstart enjoying it?
Mr. Kim: It is said that yeot dates back more than
1,000 years. Back in the old days, only the
rich could eat yeot, but nowadays, everyone
can enjoy it. It’s still popular.
Host: It has a ⓒlong history. Where did you learn
how to make yeot?
Mr. Kim: I learned it from my father and grandfather.
Our family has been making yeot for 140
years.
Host: Wow, that’s quite a long time! Could you
ⓓdescribe how to make it?
Mr. Kim: I stick to the traditional method and recipe.
First, steamed rice is mixed with barley
malt and then fermented for several hours.
After that, it is boiled to make yeot batter.
The batter is then stretched and folded
back over and over again by hand. Lastly,
it is cut into small pieces.

your work?

Aranmula, a village in India, is home to the
traditional craft of mirror making. Here, the mirrors
are made entirely of metal. With typical glass
mirrors, light has to travel through the glass in
order to get reflected on the back of the glass
coated with metal. In contrast, the Aranmula mirror
reflects light on the surface of the metal and shows
a more accurate reflection. The craft has been
passed down in Aranmula for around 500 years.
Sudhammal J learned the trade secrets from her
father when she was little, including the formula for
the perfect ratio of tin and copper to create the
mirror’s reflective surface.

body:
In Jeonju, Korea, Kim Dong-sik has been making
hapjukseons, traditional folding fans that used to be
reserved for royal families. He uses a 350-year-old
technique ⓐthat has been passed down through his
family. Although the fan looks simple, the process
of making it involves about 150 manual steps
ⓑused natural materials. It ⓒtakes four to five days
to make just one fan.
It starts with ⓓpreparing bamboo. He makes it
soft by boiling it and leaves it out to dry for up to
two weeks. Then, he splits the bamboo into strips
and thins them down again and again until you can
see through them. He then glues two strips into
one rib and binds the ribs tightly. This makes the
fan incredibly ⓔstrong. Now that the framework is
ready, he spreads the fan ribs out with glue applied
on them. Then, he carefully attaches paper to the
ribs, ⓕfolds it for each rib. Afterward, the fan may
be left plain or ⓖdecorate by a painter.
Kim says, “To make a fan, you need a lot of patience
and determination. In the old days, all the fans were
made this way. (A)온전한 전통 기법들이 학습되고 미래
에 전수될 수 있도록 저는 이것을 고수하고 있습니다.”

윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓖ 중, 어법상 어색한 것을 모두골라 짝지은 것은?
solution: ⓑ used → using (수식을 받는 150 manual steps(150 단계의 수작업 공정)가 천연 재료를 ‘사용하는’ 주체이므로 능동을 나 타내는 현재분사 using으로 고친다.) ⓕ folds → folding (동사(attaches)가 있는 완전한 절(he ~ ribs) 뒤 에 접속사 없이 콤마(,)로만 또 다른 동사가 연결될 수 없으므로 분 사구문을 이루는 분사 자리이다. 의미상 주어인 he(그)가 it(그것), 곧 종이를 살마다 ‘접는’ 주체이며 뒤에 목적어인 it이 이어지고 있으므 로 folds를 능동의 의미를 나타내는 현재분사 folding으로 고친다.) ⓖ decorate → decorated (주어 the fan이 ‘남겨지는’ 그리고 ‘장식 되는’ 대상으로 조동사 may 뒤에 이어지는 be동사의 원형 be와 함 께 수동태를 이루는 과거분사 left와 등위접속사 and로 병렬 연결되 어 있으므로 동사원형 decorate를 과거분사 decorated로 고친다.)

First of all, we need to be clear about the role of
the tongue. The information our tongues send to
our brains is very simple. We generally like
sweetness and hate bitterness, and the biological
reasons for that are deeply rooted in our brains.
For one, babies like sweet tastes, not bitter ones,
since bitterness can indicate poison. Not liking bitter
things is, in a sense, a natural defense mechanism.
Due to genetic differences, some people may be
more
sensitive
than
others
to
bitterness.
Interestingly, how sensitive you are to bitterness
doesn’t always relate to whether or not you like a
certain type of food. For example, the fact that
someone thinks celery is more bitter than other
people find it does not necessarily mean the person
can’t grow to like it. Likewise, even if you find it to
be less bitter than others do, you may still hate it.

person can’t grow to like it. Likewise, even if you
find it to be less bitter than others do, you may
still hate it.
The information our tongues convey does not,
however, paint a full picture of the world of tastes.
There are also flavors, a wider spectrum of
sensations we get from food. To ⓔappreciate

cilantro, we need not just our tongues, but more
importantly our noses. As we chew food, its smells
make their way to the back of our noses from

As a coder, Nand Vinchhi wanted to invent
something that didn’t require a mechanical device.
(A)One day, he was brainstorming with friends, and
the group came up with an idea for an app that
could translate sign language. (B)In the end, they
decided not to develop it, but Nand couldn’t stop
thinking about the translator. (C)In just a few months,
he developed an app based on artificial intelligence
for translating American Sign Language (ASL) in real
time. (D)Despite its wide use, no accurate count of
ASL users has been kept. (E)Nand’s app was
basically a speech-to-text app for sign language,
where hand movements corresponded to speech.
The hardest part was figuring out how to make
the app recognize hand gestures. At times, he felt
he was stuck. When that happened, he would go to
sleep. For Nand, ⓐsleeping on it paid off. He decided
to focus on the body parts which are important in
signing, such as individual fingertips. Using a
machine-learning program, he then taught the app
to identify those key points in the videos he took.

Cars are now making steps toward their own kind
of freedom; that is, freedom from people. The goal
is to build a car that uses artificial intelligence so
that it thinks and drives like a human. The
technology for a self-driving car has reached the
point where it is becoming increasingly accessible.
Self-driving cars have clear advantages. Most of all,
sitting behind the wheel would no longer be limited
by age or ability. ⓐ____________________, a person
who has lost sight could rely on a self-driving car
to go from one place to another. Furthermore,
most accidents are caused by careless people on
the road. For example, many crashes are caused by
people using their phones while driving, falling
asleep at the wheel, or driving while drunk. With a
self-driving car, people would not need to worry
about such situations on the road.
ⓑ____________________, there are also some serious
concerns when it comes to the safety of self-driving
cars, since the technology is still far from perfect. In
fact, a self-driving car depends only on its sensors,
GPS, and computer programs to work properly. If
any of these broke down or were used for
unintended purposes, then the safety and security
of the rider as well as other people on the road
could be put at risk.

Personal Experiences
Can we learn to like a food we’ve long disliked?
“Your biology is not your destiny. When you’re
open to different foods, you learn to like what you
eat,” answers Julie Mennella, a researcher from the
Monell Chemical Senses Center. She says that kids
are particularly adaptable when it comes to learning
to like new foods. Research has shown that after
tasting a food eight or ten times, children will
become more accepting of it. Similarly, even people
who hate cilantro may be able to learn to tolerate
it or even like it. Over time and through exposure,
they can build up tolerance to cilantro, by adding a
small amount in a curry, for example.

the tongue. The information our tongues send to
our brains is very simple. We generally like

reasons for that are deeply rooted in our brains.

when each of us interacts with people from around

today’s
global

we

more

Personal Experiences
Can we learn to like a food we’ve long disliked?
“Your biology is not your destiny. When you’re
open to different foods, you learn to like what you
eat,” answers Julie Mennella, a researcher from the
Monell Chemical Senses Center. She says that kids
are particularly adaptable when it comes to learning
to like new foods. Research has shown that after
tasting a food eight or ten times, children will
become more accepting of it. Similarly, even people
who hate cilantro may be able to learn to tolerate
it or even like it. Over time and through exposure,
they can build up tolerance to cilantro, by adding a
small amount in a curry, for example.
While preferences can be changed, usually after a
few trials, significant experiences with foods —
especially those you had when you were young —
can
have
a
lasting
effect.
Suppose
you
are
hospitalized. Confined to a bed, you get served
miyeokguk too many times. Then, you could avoid
the food for a long time. In contrast, associations
with good memories can make you like some
foods. For example, you might love sujeonggwa
simply because of a warm, happy memory of your
grandmother making it.

Repeated exposure to a food, such as beingserved miyeokguk often during hospitalization,might cause someone to avoid it for a longtime.
Sujeonggwa is generally disliked because it islinked to childhood memories.

Aranmula, a village in India, is home to the
traditional craft of mirror making. Here, the mirrors
are made (A)[entirely / partly] of metal. With typical
glass mirrors, light has to travel through the glass
in order to get reflected on the back of the glass
coated with metal. In contrast, the Aranmula mirror
reflects light on the surface of the metal and shows
a more accurate reflection. The craft has been

years. Sudhammal J learned the trade secrets from
her father when she was little, including the formula
for the (C)[perfect / imperfect] ratio of tin and
copper to create the mirror’s reflective surface.

body:
Host: Welcome to Meet the Artisans. Our guest
today is Mr. Kim Deok-man. He’s here to talk
about yeot, an old Korean treat. Mr. Kim,
could you please introduce ⓐyourself to our
viewers?
Mr. Kim: Sure. Hello, everyone! It’s great to be here.
I’m from Chungju, Korea, and specialize in
making yeot.
Host: Could you first tell us a little bit about yeot?
When did Koreans first start enjoying it?
Mr. Kim: It is said that yeot dates back more than
1,000 years. Back in the old days, only the
rich could eat yeot, but nowadays, everyone
can enjoy it. It’s still popular.
Host: It has a long history. Where did you learn
how to make yeot?
Mr. Kim: I learned it from my father and grandfather.
Our family ⓑhas been made yeot for 140 years.
Host: Wow, that’s quite a long time! Could you
describe how to make it?
Mr. Kim: I stick to the traditional method and recipe.
First, ⓒsteamed rice is mixed with barley
malt and then fermented for several hours.
After that, it is boiled to make yeot batter.
The batter is then stretched and ⓓfolded
back over and over again by hand. Lastly,
it is cut into small pieces.
Host: Interesting! What do you think is important in
your work?
Mr. Kim: I think it’s important to pass down the
traditional family yeot recipe from one
generation
to
the
next.
I’m
proudly
representing the culture and tradition, and
that pride keeps me ⓔgoing.
Host: Mr. Kim, thank you for joining us.
*barley malt 엿기름

hapjukseons, traditional folding fans that used to be
reserved for royal families. He uses a 350-year-old
technique that has been passed down through his
family. Although the fan looks simple, the process
of making it involves about 150 manual steps using
natural materials. It takes four to five days to make
just one fan.

Biology
First of all, we need to be clear about the role of
the tongue. The information our tongues send to
our brains is very simple. We generally like
sweetness and hate bitterness, and the biological
reasons for that are deeply rooted in our brains.
(A) For one, babies like sweet tastes, not bitter
ones, since bitterness can indicate poison. Not
liking bitter things is, in a sense, a natural
defense mechanism.
(B) For example, the fact that someone thinks celery
is more bitter than other people find it does
not necessarily mean the person can’t grow to
like it. Likewise, even if you find it to be less
bitter than others do, you may still hate it.
(C) Due to genetic differences, some people may be
more
sensitive
than
others
to
bitterness.
Interestingly, how sensitive you are to bitterness
doesn’t always relate to whether or not you like
a certain type of food.

promote cooperation and peace. It is practiced at
many levels. For example, when the president of a
country hosts a state dinner, the meal serves as a
symbolic gesture of welcoming and honoring the
visiting head of state. Some governments even
launch public food diplomacy campaigns, (A)[using /
use] food to promote trade or tourism. Food
diplomacy can also occur on an everyday level
when each of us (B)[interact / interacts] with people
from around the world through food, whether at a
neighborhood Vietnamese restaurant, an Indian food

Berlin. In today’s global economy, we are more

filled with large options from across the world and
restaurants (C)[serving / served] food from formerly
unreachable places. Having access to the cuisines
and cultures of the world has allowed for a better
understanding of ourselves as well as other cultures.

Food preferences vary across cultures, too. Every
culture may have something that is considered
disagreeable in other cultures. Durian fruit from
Southeast Asia or American sweet potato pie
topped with marshmallows may seem distasteful to
people not familiar with them. In fact, food
preferences in different parts of the world have a
lot to do with what is available or essential: for
instance, beans in Mexico, okra in India, and
fermented shark in Iceland. Of course, we cannot
predict food preferences solely on the basis of a
person’s cultural background, as Isabella’s case
showed with cilantro.
It is not surprising that our food preferences are
as varied as the foods we eat. Some of the
preferences are biological, and some are learned.
Given this, is it any wonder that all sorts of foods
have both fans and haters?

Personal Experiences
Can we learn to like a food we’ve long disliked?
“Your biology is not your destiny. When you’re
open to different foods, you learn to like what you
eat,” answers Julie Mennella, a researcher from the
Monell Chemical Senses Center. She says that kids
are particularly adaptable when it comes to learning
to like new foods. Research has shown that after
tasting a food eight or ten times, children will
become more accepting of it. Similarly, even people
who hate cilantro may be able to learn to tolerate
it or even like it. Over time and through exposure,
they can build up tolerance to cilantro, by adding a
small amount in a curry, for example.

kids are particularly (A)[adaptable / resistant] when

The information our tongues ⓐconveying does
not, however, paint a full picture of the world of
tastes. There are also flavors, a wider spectrum of
sensations ⓑwhich we get from food. To appreciate
flavors such as chocolate, vanilla, blue cheese, and
cilantro, we need not just our tongues, but more
importantly our noses. As we chew food, its smells
make their way to the back of our noses from
inside our mouths, ⓒenabling us to distinguish
between many flavors. Some scientists discovered
that individuals with a certain gene ⓓare more
sensitive to the smell of cilantro. These people are
likely ⓔto say it has a soapy flavor.

Food diplomacy means using food as a tool to
promote cooperation and peace. It is practiced at
many levels. For example, when the president of a
country hosts a state dinner, the meal serves as a
symbolic gesture of welcoming and honoring the
visiting head of state. Some governments even
launch public food diplomacy campaigns, using
food to promote trade or tourism. Food diplomacy
can also occur on an everyday level when each of
us interacts with people from around the world
through
food,
whether
at
a
neighborhood
Vietnamese restaurant, an Indian food truck in
Melbourne, or a Mexican taco stand in Berlin. In
today’s
global
economy,
we
are
more
interconnected than ever, with grocery store shelves
filled with large options from across the world and
restaurants serving food from formerly unreachable
places. Having access to the cuisines and cultures
of the world has allowed for a better understanding
of ourselves as well as other cultures. If you want
to learn about our global neighbors, sometimes it is
as easy as going out for dinner.

blood and then ⓑescapes quickly, leaving behind

Carbon dioxide, which humans and other animals

ⓒwhich a nice meal is near. They are highly

The women in the town of Sejnane in Tunisia, like
Aljia Saidani and her daughter, Rim, still follow the
methods of making pottery by hand that ⓐ[date /
dates] back over 3,000 years. They collect clay and
spread it out to dry for about five days under the
sun. They add broken pieces of pottery to make
the clay stronger. The mixture is molded into a
shape ⓑ[which / how] comes to mind on the spot.
Then, the piece is ⓒ[coating / coated] with white
clay or red earth. Next, it is fired over an open
flame. Then, it is finally time to decorate it. All the
colors come from nature, and the designs give the
pottery its unique look.

The work is tough, and the craft has been avoided
by young people. However, Rim says, “It has made
me a more patient person. Everything about it
needs to be done step by step. Everything is in
slow motion. This is actually a life lesson that I
really cherish.”

could you please introduce yourself to our

I’m from Chungju, Korea, and specialize in
making yeot.

When did Koreans first start enjoying it?

1,000 years. Back in the old days, only the
rich
could
eat
yeot,

it
from
my

and
grandfather.

family
has
been
making yeot for 140 years.

body:
In Jeonju, Korea, Kim Dong-sik has been making
hapjukseons, traditional folding fans that used to be
reserved for royal families. He uses a 350-year-old
technique that has been passed down through his
family. Although the fan looks simple, the process
of making it involves about 150 manual steps using
natural materials. It takes four to five days to make
just one fan.
It starts with preparing bamboo. He makes it soft
by boiling it and leaves it out to dry for up to two
weeks. Then, he splits the bamboo into strips and
thins them down again and again until you can see
through them. He then glues two strips into one
rib and binds the ribs tightly. This makes the fan
incredibly strong. (A)이제 틀이 준비되었으니, 그것들
위에 풀이 발린 채로 그는 부챗살을 펼친다. Then, he
carefully attaches paper to the ribs, folding it for
each rib. Afterward, the fan may be left plain or
decorated by a painter.
Kim says, “To make a fan, you need a lot of
patience and determination. In the old days, all the
fans were made this way. I stand by this so that
the perfect traditional skills can be taught and
carried into the future.”

윗글의 제목으로 알맞은 것은?
choices: The Decline of Traditional Craftsmanship
The Life Philosophy of Handicraft Masters
The Patience and Craftsmanship Behind Hapjukseons
Master of the Hapjukseon Training His YoungerStudents
The Quality of a Hapjukseon Depends on theBamboo Used
solution: 가문 대대로 내려오는 350년 된 기법을 사용하여 150 단계의 수작업 공정을 거쳐 합죽선을 만드는 세심한 과정과 합죽선을 만들려면 상당한 인내심과 결의가 필요하다는 김동식 씨의 말 을 통해 합죽선 뒤에는 인내와 장인 정신이 숨어 있음을 시사 한 내용이므로, ❸ ‘합죽선 뒤의 인내와 장인 정신’이 제목으로 알맞다.

Earthworms are a great addition to your garden as
well. They help keep your soil soft and breathable
by digging tunnels that bring air to the roots of
plants. They also eat the dead bits of plants that
fall to the ground, recycling them back into the soil
and helping new plants to grow. ⓐ_________________,
their waste makes your soil richer, and they are
excellent at breaking down organic matter in your
garden. ⓑ_________________, you should be careful
about applying artificial fertilizers to your garden
after introducing earthworms. They will find a new
home when the soil around them changes.

윗글의 빈칸 ⓐ, ⓑ에 들어갈 말로 알맞게 연결된 것은?

ⓐ
ⓑ
choices: What’s moreEven so
That isTherefore
In additionIn short
In other wordsHowever
BesidesAs a result
solution: ⓐ 지렁이가 식물의 죽은 부분들을 흙으로 재순환시켜 새로운 식물이 자라도록 돕는다는 내용 뒤에 지렁이가 정원에 제공하 는 또 다른 도움으로, 지렁이의 배설물은 토양을 더 비옥하게 만든다는 내용이 추가되고 있으므로, 빈칸에는 ‘게다가’를 뜻하 는 What’s more, In addition, Besides가 알맞다. ⓑ 정원에 있는 유기물을 분해하는 데에 탁월하다는 지렁이의 긍정적 역할을 설명한 뒤에 인공 비료를 사용하면 지렁이가 새로운 서식지를 찾을 수 있으므로 조심해야 한다는 역접 관 계의 내용이 연결되므로, ‘그렇기는 하지만’을 뜻하는 Even so 나 ‘그러나’를 뜻하는 However가 알맞다.

body:
If you had to choose our greatest predator in
nature, which would you pick? Sharks, lions, or bears?
According to history professor Timothy Winegard, it is
actually the mosquito. Mosquitoes can pass on ⓐ[fatal
/ mild] diseases like malaria and yellow fever. Over a
million people worldwide die of these diseases every
year. Throughout history, Winegard estimates that
mosquitoes have killed more people than any other
single cause — about fifty-two billion people, nearly
half of all humans who have ever lived.
Winegard claims that mosquitoes also played a role
in shaping the history of several countries. Take the
Roman Empire, for example. The fall of the Western
Roman Empire was ⓑ[immediate / progressive],
spanning over centuries.
(A) On the one hand, mosquitoes helped protect
the city against the armies coming to attack it.
However, they eventually spread the disease not
only throughout the city, but also throughout
the empire, crushing much of the population.
(B) Rome, the capital of the empire, was once
surrounded by a huge stretch of wetland. This
was a(n) ⓒ[adverse / flawless] breeding ground
for mosquitoes and hence a hot spot for malaria.
(C) Here are commonly cited reasons for the fall of
the empire: invasions by outside forces, economic
troubles, and corruption. Diseases like malaria,
however, also contributed.

윗글의 괄호 ⓐ, ⓑ, ⓒ에서 흐름상 알맞은 말로 바르게 연결된 것은?

ⓐ
ⓑ
ⓒ
choices: mildprogressiveflawless
fatalprogressiveadverse
mildimmediateadverse
fatalprogressiveflawless
fatalimmediateadverse
solution: ⓐ 모기가 옮기는 말라리아와 황열 같은 질병으로 매년 전 세 계를 통틀어 백만 명이 넘는 사람들이 사망한다는 내용이 이 어지므로, 모기가 치명적인 질병을 옮긴다는 흐름으로 fatal(치 명적인, 죽음을 초래하는)이 알맞다. ⓑ 여러 세기에 걸쳤다는 내용이 이어지므로, 서로마 제국의 몰락은 점진적으로 일어났다는 흐름으로 progressive(점진적인)가 알맞다. ⓒ 말라리아의 창궐지였다는 내용이 이어지므로, 습지가 모기에게 완 벽한 번식지였다는 흐름으로 flawless(완벽한, 흠 하나 없는)가 알맞다.

Earthworms are a great addition to your garden as
well. They help keep your soil soft and breathable
by digging tunnels that bring air to the roots of
plants. They also eat the dead bits of plants that
fall to the ground, recycling them back into the soil
and helping new plants to grow. Moreover, their
waste makes your soil richer, and they are excellent
at breaking down organic matter in your garden.
However, you should be careful about applying
artificial fertilizers to your garden after introducing
earthworms. They will find a new home when the
soil around them changes.
